verdict.rationale: Rootly documents hosted public and private status pages. A custom domain is implied because the docs describe a public JSON API served on the status page's custom domain. An API endpoint posts status-page events from an incident, which ties the page to incident state. However, the evidence pack has nothing on subscriber notifications, a core part of the story. Missing for 10: documented subscriber/email/SMS notifications for status page updates, explicit custom-domain setup docs, documented automatic incident-to-status-page sync, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, I can publish a hosted public status page — custom domain, subscriber notifications — driven from incident state

citations.quote: Rootly has two types of status pages available: public status pages and private status pages.
Rootly exposes a public JSON API on your status page's custom domain
Status pages allow you to quickly communicate information about the health of your services and applications to internal stakeholders and external customers.
